title: WildinSync - eDNA Sampling of Surfaces
author: David Racine
materials: Always wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): disposable nitrile gloves during sampling, subsampling, and equipment handling. Replace gloves between sampling transects and whenever they become contaminated. Wear long sleeves and closed footwear suitable for fieldwork conditions. Do not leave ethanol, bleach, or used consumables in the field and pack out all waste. When ethanol and bleach come into contact, they can generate toxic chloroform vapors. Proper PPE use is essential to reduce the risk of chemical burns caused by bleach and other hazardous reagents.

steps.title: Prepare Sampling Workspace
steps.instruction: Establish a clean preparation area using a plastic tray and sanitized equipment.

substeps.instruction: Put on gloves from the additional glove box.
Clean the plastic tray with bleach and paper towels.
Wipe the plastic tray with DNA-free water (or 80% ethanol if DNA-free water is unavailable) to remove bleach residue; ensure bleach has dried before using ethanol to avoid toxic chloroform vapors.
Clean the outside of the swabbing and buffer kits with bleach and place them on the tray.
Clean scissors and a permanent marker (with cap closed) with bleach, let dry, and wipe with DNA-free water or 80% ethanol.
Place the cleaned scissors and marker on the tray.

steps.title: Map and Define Sampling Site
steps.instruction: Identify site features and establish transects within a 1 ha plot.

substeps.instruction: Identify features (vegetation, rocks, dead wood, bare soil, buildings, concrete, asphalt), map the site, and take overview pictures.
Define four non-overlapping 100 m transects (T1, T2, T3, T4) that maximize vegetation coverage and represent overall ground cover composition.
Mark the start and end of transects using field sticks or permanent markers/coordinates for long-term monitoring.
Avoid walking within the sampling site until sampling begins to prevent eDNA contamination.

steps.title: Prepare Swabbing Materials
steps.instruction: Open the sampling kits and don sterile gloves for each transect.

substeps.instruction: Place a marker (e.g., a flag) at the start of the first transect.
Using scissors and the initial pair of gloves, open the swabbing kit and the buffer kit; leave both on the tray.
Remove the first pair of gloves from the swabbing kit and put them on, ensuring you do not touch the exterior of the gloves or other kit contents with bare hands.

steps.title: Collect eDNA Samples
steps.instruction: Perform surface swabbing at designated intervals along the transect.

substeps.instruction: Remove the swab and tube of DNA-free water from the swabbing kit without touching the kit's exterior.
Moisten the swab with half of the DNA-free water.

At 10 points every ten meters along the transect, swab soil litter (avoiding dirt), stems, leaves, flowers, and other relevant surfaces within a 2 meter radius (excluding the area behind you) for 45 seconds per point.
If the swab dries out at the fifth point, re-wet it with the remaining water; otherwise, do not re-wet.
Repeat this entire process for the remaining 3 transects to obtain a total of 4 samples per site.

steps.title: Preserve and Label Samples
steps.instruction: Transfer the swab to the buffer tube and secure the sample.

substeps.instruction: Return to the clean tray and remove the buffer tube from the buffer kit without touching the kit's exterior.
Place the swab into the buffer tube, close tightly, and shake vigorously for 10 seconds.
Label the buffer tube.
Place the labeled tube into a ziplock plastic bag, label the bag, and close it.
Remove and dispose of gloves.
Record the label in the metadata and complete the metadata sheet.

steps.title: Store Samples
steps.instruction: Store the labeled buffer tubes in a dry room temperature environment away from light until extraction.

substeps.instruction: Ensure samples are NOT stored in a refrigerator or freezer, as this is strictly prohibited.
